title: Effect of low-dose hydrocortisone and inhaled nitric oxide on inflammatory mediators and local pulmonary metalloproteinases activity in LPS-induced sepsis in piglets
authors: Kiczak, L., Pasławska, U., Goździk, W., et al.
abstract: Hospital mortality in sepsis varies between 30–45%. We explored the anti-inflammatory effect of a double-treatment strategy (inhaled nitric oxide [iNO] + low-dose hydrocortisone) on the lungs in a long-term porcine endotoxic shock model. A shock-like condition was established in 23 piglets by continuous intravenous infusion of E. coli lipopolysaccharide (LPS) for 10 h. Twelve pigs received iNO and hydrocortisone, while 11 pigs were vehicle controls. Pigs treated with iNO and hydrocortisone displayed less pulmonary inflammatory infiltrates, lower levels of IL-1β, decreased proMMP2, and reduced active MMP9. We demonstrated that in a porcine endotoxemia model, NO inhalation combined with intravenous hydrocortisone led to the attenuation of the inflammatory cascade induced by bacterial LPS.
rationale: Model violation: Sepsis was induced exclusively by continuous intravenous infusion of E. coli lipopolysaccharide (LPS / endotoxin). Our protocol strictly excludes all pure LPS/endotoxin challenge models.
learning_pearl: 🚨 The #1 Trap: Researchers love endotoxemia models, but pure LPS infusion is strictly EXCLUDED under EX-LPS, even in large mammals like piglets!

title: Adjunctive granisetron therapy in patients with sepsis or septic shock (GRANTISS): A single-center, single-blinded, randomized, controlled clinical trial
authors: Guan, J., Liao, Y., Guo, Y., et al.
abstract: Background: In preclinical experiments, the 5-HT3 receptor antagonist granisetron reduced inflammation and improved survival in septic mice. This randomized controlled trial was designed to assess the efficacy and safety of granisetron in human patients with sepsis. Methods: Adult patients with sepsis and procalcitonin ≥ 2 ng/ml were randomized 1:1 to receive intravenous granisetron (3 mg every 8 h) or normal saline for 4 days. The primary outcome was 28-day all-cause mortality. Results: The modified intention-to-treat analysis included 150 septic patients. The 28-day all-cause mortalities in granisetron and placebo groups were 34.7% and 35.6%, respectively (odds ratio, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.49–1.89). Conclusion: Granisetron did not improve 28-day mortality in human patients with sepsis.
rationale: Population violation: This is a clinical trial conducted in 150 human adult ICU patients with sepsis. Our systematic review only includes preclinical mammalian animal models -> EX-CLINICAL.
learning_pearl: 🚨 Clinical Paper Trap: Clinical trials in human patients are excluded under EX-CLINICAL because our protocol is strictly limited to preclinical mammalian laboratory animal models (mice, rats, pigs, sheep, etc.).

title: Administration of mesenchymal stem cell secretome improves survival and dampens cytokine storm in murine fecal pellet peritonitis
authors: Chavez, M. A., Gomez, A., Torres, L., et al.
abstract:
Background: Cell-free therapies utilizing stem cell conditioned medium (secretome) avoid immunological risks of live cell transplantation. We tested MSC secretome in a fecal pellet peritonitis model.
Methods: Male Balb/c mice received an intraperitoneal implantation of a standardized fecal pellet (0.5 mL) to generate polymicrobial peritonitis. Two hours later, mice received tail-vein injections of concentrated MSC secretome or vehicle saline. Peritoneal bacterial load, serum IL-10, TNF-α, and 5-day survival were recorded.
Results: MSC secretome treated mice exhibited enhanced bacterial clearance, elevated systemic IL-10 levels, attenuated lung vascular leak, and improved 5-day survival (58% vs 22%, p = 0.007).
Conclusion: Stem cell secretome acts as a potent therapeutic agent in polymicrobial abdominal sepsis.
rationale: Clear INCLUDE: Live mammalian mice, established polymicrobial sepsis model (fecal pellet peritonitis), therapeutic intervention (MSC secretome) administered post-induction, survival and bacterial clearance outcomes assessed, primary empirical research.
learning_pearl: Fecal Pellet Peritonitis Trap: Inoculation of fecal pellets into the peritoneal cavity is an established, approved live-pathogen polymicrobial sepsis model (not pure LPS!). Because an intervention is tested in live mice with survival outcomes, it is a textbook INCLUDE.

title: Pre-treatment with resveratrol alleviates acute lung injury and suppresses HMGB1 release in rat cecal ligation and puncture
authors: Kovaleva, O., Smirnova, T., Petrov, A., et al.
abstract:
Background: Sepsis-induced acute lung injury is propagated by late inflammatory mediators such as high mobility group box 1 (HMGB1). We investigated prophylactic resveratrol in septic rats.
Methods: Sprague-Dawley rats received resveratrol (30 mg/kg/day orally) for 5 days preceding medium-grade CLP. Arterial oxygenation, lung wet-to-dry ratios, serum HMGB1, and lung histology were assessed 24 hours post-CLP.
Results: Rats pre-treated with resveratrol maintained significantly higher PaO2/FiO2 ratios (380 vs 210 mmHg, p < 0.001), had lower lung wet-to-dry ratios, and reduced circulating HMGB1 levels.
Conclusions: Prophylactic resveratrol preserves pulmonary barrier integrity in rat CLP sepsis.
rationale: Valid INCLUDE: In vivo mammalian rats, approved polymicrobial sepsis model (cecal ligation and puncture / CLP), evaluates therapeutic/prophylactic intervention (resveratrol) administered prior to CLP. Guidelines state: interventions given before or after induction are included!
learning_pearl: Prophylactic vs Therapeutic Timing: Interventions administered prior to or during sepsis induction (pre-treatments like resveratrol before CLP) ARE INCLUDED under our protocol as long as they evaluate potential benefit on sepsis outcomes in an approved in vivo animal model.

title: Nordihydroguaiaretic acid reduces secondary organ injury in septic rats after cecal ligation and puncture
authors: Zubrow, M. E., Margulies, S. S., Yehya, N.
abstract: Background: Sepsis is characterized by dysregulated host inflammation and oxidative stress leading to multi-organ dysfunction. Nordihydroguaiaretic acid (NDGA) is a plant-derived antioxidant and 5-lipoxygenase inhibitor. We hypothesized that NDGA attenuates organ injury and improves survival in experimental abdominal sepsis. Methods: Male Sprague-Dawley rats underwent cecal ligation and double puncture (CLP). Rats were randomized to receive NDGA (20 mg/kg intraperitoneally) or vehicle 1 hour post-CLP. Systemic hemodynamics, plasma cytokines, renal injury (serum creatinine, BUN), hepatic enzymes (ALT, AST), and 36-hour survival were assessed. Results: NDGA treatment significantly improved 36-hour survival following CLP compared with vehicle controls (65% vs 25%, p = 0.014). NDGA-treated septic rats exhibited significantly blunted plasma TNF-α and IL-6, attenuated acute kidney injury, and reduced hepatocellular vacuolization. Conclusion: Delayed administration of NDGA reduces secondary organ injury and enhances survival in rat polymicrobial CLP sepsis.
rationale: Clear INCLUDE: Live mammalian rats, approved polymicrobial sepsis model (cecal ligation and puncture / CLP), therapeutic intervention (NDGA) evaluated after induction, organ and survival outcomes assessed, primary study published in 2020.
learning_pearl: Textbook INCLUDE! Live mammals + surgical CLP model + active pharmacological intervention + survival/organ outcomes.

title: The effects of the pulsed magnetic field on sepsis-induced liver tissue injury in rats
authors: Gevrek, F., Yelli, S., Gürgül, S.
abstract: Objective: Sepsis causes life-threatening systemic inflammation and multi-organ failure, with liver dysfunction being a major determinant of mortality. We investigated whether pulsed magnetic field (PMF) application protects against sepsis-induced hepatic injury in a rodent model. Methods: Twenty-eight adult Wistar albino rats were divided into Sham, PMF-treated, and CLP Sepsis groups. Abdominal polymicrobial sepsis was induced by cecal ligation and puncture (CLP). Septic rats were exposed to therapeutic PMF regimens (1.5 mT, 40 Hz) post-surgery. Liver histopathology, sinusoidal dilatation, inflammatory cell infiltration, and apoptotic markers (active caspase-3, Bax, and Bcl-2) were quantified. Results: CLP induced extensive hepatocyte necrosis, congestion, and elevated caspase-3 expression. Rats treated with therapeutic PMF displayed significantly preserved hepatic microarchitecture, reduced inflammatory infiltrates, and downregulated apoptotic Bax/caspase-3 signaling (p < 0.01). Conclusion: Non-invasive pulsed magnetic field therapy attenuates hepatic injury and apoptosis in rat polymicrobial sepsis.
rationale: Valid INCLUDE: Live in vivo rats, approved CLP sepsis model, evaluates a therapeutic intervention (pulsed magnetic field physical therapy) hypothesized to be beneficial, assesses hepatic injury outcomes, primary study from 2023.
learning_pearl: Our protocol includes ANY therapy or intervention hypothesized to be beneficial for sepsis—including physical and non-pharmacological modalities like pulsed magnetic fields paired with CLP!

title: Zebrafish GSDMEb Cleavage-Gated Pyroptosis Drives Septic Acute Kidney Injury In Vivo
authors: Wang, Y., Gao, W., Shi, X., et al.
abstract: Gasdermin-mediated pyroptosis plays a crucial role in antibacterial defense, yet excessive pyroptosis triggers lethal septic organ failure. Here, we investigated the molecular executors of septic acute kidney injury (AKI) in a live zebrafish (Danio rerio) model. We identified that caspy2 and gasdermin Eb (GSDMEb) mediate systemic inflammation and renal tubular cell death upon septic challenge. Activated caspy2 specifically cleaved GSDMEb to release its pore-forming N-terminal domain. Treatment with the specific peptide inhibitor Ac-FEID-CMK significantly blocked GSDMEb cleavage, prevented renal tubular pyroptosis, and rescued septic zebrafish from mortality. These findings establish that GSDMEb-dependent pyroptosis drives septic acute kidney injury in zebrafish.
rationale: Organism violation: The study is conducted entirely in zebrafish (Danio rerio). Our eligibility protocol strictly restricts the population to in vivo mammalian models (mice, rats, pigs, sheep, rabbits, etc.) and excludes non-mammalian organisms.
learning_pearl: Non-mammalian model trap: Zebrafish (Danio rerio), fruit flies (Drosophila), and nematodes (C. elegans) are excluded under EX-NOT-INVIVO, even when studying sepsis genes in vivo!

title: Agar pellet implantation model of Bacteroides fragilis and Escherichia coli abdominal sepsis in rats: Therapeutic impact of metronidazole and ceftriaxone
authors: Kassianos, G., Papavramidis, T. S., Kotzampassi, K.
abstract:
Background: Agar pellet encapsulation permits sustained, localized bacterial release simulating perforated appendicitis abscesses. We evaluated metronidazole plus ceftriaxone in this polymicrobial model.
Methods: Wistar rats received intraperitoneal implantation of a standardized agar pellet containing live Bacteroides fragilis (10^8 CFU) and E. coli (10^7 CFU). Twelve hours later, rats received intraperitoneal metronidazole (30 mg/kg) and ceftriaxone (50 mg/kg) or vehicle control for 5 days. Abscess formation, blood bacteremia, and survival were recorded.
Results: Antibiotic treatment eliminated systemic bacteremia, contained abscess encapsulation, and improved 7-day survival from 25% to 80% (p < 0.001).
Conclusions: Combination antimicrobial therapy effectively treats polymicrobial agar pellet peritonitis.
rationale: Clear INCLUDE: In vivo mammalian rats, approved agar pellet implantation model with live pathogens (B. fragilis + E. coli), therapeutic antibiotic intervention, assessed survival and bacteremia, published research.
learning_pearl: Agar pellet implantation models: Inoculation or pellet implantation containing live bacterial pathogens into the peritoneal cavity is an established, approved in vivo mammalian sepsis model!

title: MiR-702-3p inhibits the inflammatory injury in septic H9c2 cells by regulating NOD1
authors: Liu, C., Yang, Y., Liang, G., Zhang, A., Xu, F.
abstract: Background: Myocardial dysfunction is a severe complication of sepsis. MicroRNAs are critical post-transcriptional regulators in inflammatory responses. Here, we investigated the regulatory role of miR-702-3p in sepsis-induced cardiac myocyte injury in vitro. Methods: H9c2 embryonic rat cardiomyocyte cell lines were stimulated with LPS (1 μg/mL) to establish an in vitro cellular model of septic injury. H9c2 cells were transfected with miR-702-3p mimics or inhibitors. Cell viability (CCK-8), LDH release, and inflammatory cytokine secretion (TNF-α, IL-6) were evaluated. Dual-luciferase reporter assays verified the direct binding of miR-702-3p to the 3'-UTR of NOD1. Results: MiR-702-3p overexpression significantly suppressed NOD1 expression, enhanced cardiomyocyte viability, and decreased TNF-α and IL-6 release. Conclusion: MiR-702-3p attenuates inflammatory injury in septic H9c2 cardiomyocytes by targeting NOD1.
rationale: In vitro model violation: This study was performed entirely on cultured H9c2 rat cardiomyocyte cell lines in petri dishes without any live animal in vivo experimentation.
learning_pearl: Cell line trap: Watch out for cultured cells like H9c2, RAW 264.7, or isolated cardiomyocytes. Without live whole animals, exclude under EX-NOT-INVIVO!

title: Therapeutic Potential of Antimicrobial Peptide PN5 against Multidrug-Resistant E. coli and Anti-Inflammatory Activity in a Septic Mouse Model
authors: Cho, J. H., Kim, E. Y., Lee, B. H., et al.
abstract: Multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacterial infections pose a grave clinical threat in systemic sepsis. We evaluated the therapeutic potential of PN5, an antimicrobial peptide derived from Pinus densiflora, against lethal systemic Escherichia coli infection in vivo. Male ICR mice were challenged with intraperitoneal inoculation of clinical MDR E. coli isolates to establish acute polymicrobial bacteremic sepsis. Mice were treated with intravenous PN5 (5 or 10 mg/kg) or vehicle 1 hour post-inoculation. PN5 treatment significantly reduced bacterial colony counts in blood, spleen, and peritoneal lavage by > 3 logs (p < 0.001) and elevated 7-day survival from 15% to 70%. In addition, PN5 blunted systemic TNF-α and IL-1β secretion and attenuated acute pulmonary alveolar damage. These findings establish PN5 as a potent antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory candidate for live-pathogen bacterial sepsis.
rationale: Valid INCLUDE: In vivo mammalian mice, approved live bacterial pathogen sepsis model (MDR E. coli inoculation causing bacteremia and peritonitis), evaluated therapeutic intervention (peptide PN5), assessed bacterial clearance and 7-day survival, primary study published in 2022.
learning_pearl: Live pathogen sepsis: When bacterial inoculation (e.g. live E. coli, Klebsiella, Pseudomonas) is paired with systemic bacteremia/sepsis and an intervention is tested, it is an automatic INCLUDE!

title: The effect of thyme essential oil and endothelial progenitor stem cells on lipopolysaccharide-induced sepsis in C57BL/6 mice
authors: Khater, M., Mansour, M., El-Kafrawy, S., et al.
abstract: Sepsis triggers catastrophic endothelial barrier breakdown and multi-organ failure. We investigated the synergistic therapeutic efficacy of thyme (Thymus vulgaris) essential oil and bone marrow-derived endothelial progenitor stem cells (EPCs) in endotoxemia-induced acute sepsis. Male C57BL/6 mice were challenged with intraperitoneal injection of Escherichia coli lipopolysaccharide (LPS, 10 mg/kg) to induce septic shock. Mice were treated with thyme essential oil (50 mg/kg orally), EPCs (1 × 10^6 cells intravenously), or combination therapy 2 h post-challenge. Systemic inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6), vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), lung histopathology, and 72-hour survival were measured. Combination treatment significantly suppressed circulating TNF-α and IL-6 levels, repaired pulmonary microvascular integrity, and enhanced 72-hour survival compared with vehicle controls. These findings indicate that thyme essential oil combined with EPCs mitigates endotoxemia-induced vascular damage in mice.
rationale: Model violation: Sepsis was induced exclusively by intraperitoneal injection of bacterial lipopolysaccharide (LPS, 10 mg/kg). Pure endotoxin/LPS challenge models are strictly excluded under EX-LPS, regardless of how promising the tested stem cell or herbal therapy may be.
learning_pearl: 🚨 Endotoxin Challenge Trap: Even when an exciting therapy like endothelial progenitor stem cells or essential oils is tested in mice, if sepsis is induced by pure LPS injection, it MUST be excluded under EX-LPS!

title: Resolvin D1 protects against sepsis-induced cardiac injury in mice
authors: Wang, M., Liu, M., Zhang, J., et al.
abstract: Sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy is a critical determinant of sepsis lethality. Resolvin D1 (RvD1) is an endogenous specialized pro-resolving lipid mediator with potent tissue-protective properties. In this study, we investigated the protective mechanisms of RvD1 on septic myocardial dysfunction in vivo. Male C57BL/6 mice were challenged with intraperitoneal injection of lipopolysaccharide (LPS, 10 mg/kg) to induce endotoxemia-associated cardiac injury. Septic mice received intravenous RvD1 (100 ng/mouse) or vehicle immediately post-challenge. Cardiac function was monitored by echocardiography, and myocardial apoptosis, neutrophil infiltration (myeloperoxidase), and NF-κB/MAPK signaling were assessed. RvD1 administration significantly restored left ventricular ejection fraction, attenuated cardiac troponin I release, decreased myocardial apoptosis, and suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokine expression. Our findings reveal that Resolvin D1 protects against endotoxemic cardiac injury through inhibition of excessive inflammatory pathways.
rationale: Model violation: The study utilizes an intraperitoneal LPS endotoxemia challenge model in mice to study septic cardiomyopathy. Endotoxin-only challenges lack viable replicating pathogens and are excluded under EX-LPS.
learning_pearl: Cardiac injury in sepsis: Resolvins and pro-resolving mediators are active areas of research, but always verify the induction method. Sepsis induced via LPS injection alone is excluded under EX-LPS.

title: Neuroprotective effects of annexin A1 tripeptide in rats with sepsis-associated encephalopathy
authors: Cui, Q., Qin, N., Zhang, Y., et al.
abstract: Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) causes profound cognitive impairment and brain mitochondrial dysfunction. We explored the therapeutic effects and molecular mechanisms of the bioactive annexin A1 tripeptide (ANXA1sp) in a rodent model of septic encephalopathy. Adult Sprague-Dawley rats received intraperitoneal lipopolysaccharide (LPS, 5 mg/kg) to induce sepsis-related neuroinflammation. Rats were randomized to receive ANXA1sp (1 mg/kg) or vehicle intraperitoneally. Cognitive performance was evaluated using Morris water maze and Y-maze tests, and hippocampal mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP), reactive oxygen species (ROS), and PPAR-γ signaling were analyzed. ANXA1sp significantly attenuated LPS-induced cognitive deficits, reduced hippocampal IL-6 and TNF-α secretion, and preserved mitochondrial ATP synthesis via PPAR-γ activation. In conclusion, annexin A1 tripeptide exerts potent neuroprotection in an experimental LPS encephalopathy rat model.
rationale: Model violation: Sepsis-associated encephalopathy was modeled solely by intraperitoneal injection of lipopolysaccharide (LPS) in rats. Exclude under EX-LPS.
learning_pearl: Encephalopathy & Brain Sepsis: Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) papers frequently use LPS injections. Check the Methods section carefully—if only LPS is injected without live bacteria or surgical peritonitis, code EX-LPS.

title: PPARγ-Dependent Pioglitazone Treatment Suppresses Neuroinflammation and Improves Cognition in Sepsis-Associated Encephalopathy in Mice
authors: Zhang, J., Wang, P., Li, N., Gao, Y.
abstract: Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) is characterized by diffuse brain neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier (BBB) breakdown, and persistent cognitive deficits. In this study, we investigated the therapeutic utility of pioglitazone (Pio), a peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARγ) agonist, in an authentic mouse model of surgical sepsis. Male C57BL/6 mice underwent cecal ligation and puncture (CLP). Mice were treated with pioglitazone (10 mg/kg orally) or vehicle beginning 2 h post-surgery. BBB permeability was quantified via Evans blue dye extravasation and tight-junction claudin-5 expression. Cognitive functioning was assessed via novel object recognition and Barnes maze testing. Pioglitazone treatment significantly improved 10-day survival (from 25% to 60%, p < 0.01), preserved BBB ultrastructure, reduced microglial activation, and attenuated hippocampal neuronal apoptosis. Co-administration of the PPARγ antagonist GW9662 abolished these neuroprotective benefits, confirming a PPARγ-dependent mechanism. Pioglitazone is a promising neurotherapeutic for polymicrobial sepsis-associated encephalopathy.
rationale: Clear INCLUDE: In vivo mammalian mice, approved surgical sepsis model (cecal ligation and puncture / CLP), evaluates therapeutic intervention (pioglitazone) post-induction, assesses survival, cognitive, and BBB outcomes, primary empirical study from 2026.
learning_pearl: SAE with Surgical CLP = INCLUDE! Contrast this paper directly with Paper #13: both study sepsis encephalopathy, but Paper #13 used pure LPS (EXCLUDE), whereas Paper #14 used surgical CLP in live mice (INCLUDE)!

title: Evaluation of the protective role of resveratrol against sepsis caused by LPS via TLR4/NF-κB/TNF-α signaling pathways: Experimental study
authors: Kocak, M. B., Alver, A., Kucuk, A., et al.
abstract: Sepsis remains a life-threatening systemic syndrome characterized by hyperinflammation and oxidative injury. Resveratrol is a natural polyphenolic compound with established anti-inflammatory and free-radical scavenging properties. Here, we evaluated whether resveratrol confers organ protection in an experimental model of lipopolysaccharide-induced sepsis. Adult male Wistar albino rats were allocated into control, sepsis, and resveratrol-treated sepsis groups. Septic shock was induced by a single intraperitoneal injection of lipopolysaccharide (LPS, 5 mg/kg). Resveratrol (30 mg/kg) was administered intraperitoneally 30 min following LPS challenge. Serum TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6, as well as renal and hepatic histopathological damage and TLR4/NF-κB p65 expressions, were examined 6 h post-injection. Resveratrol significantly dampened peak serum cytokine levels, suppressed TLR4 and phosphorylated NF-κB expression in liver and kidneys, and mitigated multi-organ histological injury. These results demonstrate that resveratrol blunts LPS-induced inflammatory injury via TLR4/NF-κB inhibition.
rationale: Model violation: Sepsis was generated by single intraperitoneal injection of lipopolysaccharide (LPS, 5 mg/kg) in rats. Excluded under EX-LPS.
learning_pearl: Contrast with Training Paper #4: Resveratrol tested in rat CLP is an INCLUDE (Paper #4), but Resveratrol tested in rat LPS injection is an EXCLUDE under EX-LPS (Paper #15)! The disease model dictates eligibility!

title: Regulatory Role of Noncoding RNA in Sepsis and Sepsis-Associated Organ Dysfunction: An Updated Systematic Review
authors: Zhao, Y., Chen, Z., Tang, H., et al.
abstract: Noncoding RNAs (ncRNAs), including microRNAs, long noncoding RNAs, and circular RNAs, have emerged as pivotal epigenetic orchestrators in the pathophysiology of sepsis and sepsis-associated acute organ dysfunction. We conducted a comprehensive systematic review following PRISMA guidelines to synthesize preclinical and clinical evidence on regulatory ncRNAs in sepsis. Databases (PubMed, Web of Science, Embase) were searched up to December 2021. Eighty-two studies examining ncRNA expression profiles and functional interventions in animal models (CLP, bacterial injection) and septic ICU patient cohorts were evaluated. Pooled qualitative analysis highlights that specific microRNAs (e.g., miR-146a, miR-223) and lncRNAs (MALAT1, NEAT1) directly modulate TLR/NF-κB signaling, macrophage polarization, endothelial permeability, and septic cardiomyopathy. We discuss current diagnostic utility and therapeutic delivery challenges for ncRNA-based sepsis therapeutics.
rationale: Study design violation: This is a systematic review synthesizing 82 previously published studies, not an original primary empirical experimental laboratory report.
learning_pearl: Review Literature Trap: Even when a systematic review synthesizes in vivo animal models (like CLP), the publication itself is secondary synthesis literature and must be excluded under EX-NONPRIMARY!

title: Efficacy and Safety of Neostigmine Adjunctive Therapy in Patients With Sepsis or Septic Shock: A Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: Zheng, R., Wang, H., Lu, X., et al.
abstract: Objective: The cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway suppresses systemic inflammation via alpha-7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors. We conducted a prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial to determine whether the acetylcholinesterase inhibitor neostigmine reduces mortality and inflammatory biomarkers in human patients with sepsis. Methods: 120 adult ICU patients diagnosed with sepsis or septic shock according to Sepsis-3 criteria were randomized to receive continuous intravenous infusion of neostigmine (0.5 mg/h) or placebo for 7 days alongside standard sepsis bundle therapy. Primary endpoint was 28-day all-cause mortality; secondary endpoints included SOFA score evolution, duration of mechanical ventilation, and serum IL-6 and procalcitonin levels. Results: 28-day mortality was 23.3% in the neostigmine group versus 28.3% in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.40–1.62; p = 0.55). Neostigmine was associated with significantly accelerated resolution of GI dysfunction and reduced IL-6 levels on day 3. Conclusion: Adjunctive neostigmine did not significantly improve 28-day mortality in adult patients with sepsis or septic shock.
rationale: Population violation: This is a randomized controlled trial performed in 120 adult human ICU patients with sepsis, not an experimental laboratory animal study.
learning_pearl: Clinical Trial Trap: Whenever participants are human ICU patients, clinical trial subjects, or clinical registry cohorts, code EX-CLINICAL immediately. Our review is strictly limited to preclinical mammalian laboratory animals!

title: Avidin is evolutionarily conserved in fish but dispensable for development and resistance against Streptococcus agalactiae in zebrafish
authors: Takala, K. E., Niskanen, E. A., Saralahti, A., et al.
abstract: Avidin is a well-known egg white protein with extraordinary biotin-binding affinity, postulated to function as an innate immune defense factor against bacterial pathogens. Here, we investigated whether the avidin gene homologue in teleost fish confers in vivo protective immunity against bacterial infection using a live zebrafish (Danio rerio) model. Avidin-deficient (avd-/-) zebrafish knockout lines were generated via CRISPR/Cas9 mutagenesis. Adult and larval zebrafish were challenged with systemic microinjection of live Streptococcus agalactiae to simulate acute bacterial bacteremia and sepsis. Survival curves, bacterial loads, and innate immune gene transcript levels were monitored. Avd-/- zebrafish showed normal embryonic development and, surprisingly, exhibited no significant difference in bacterial burden or 96-hour post-infection mortality compared to wild-type controls. These results demonstrate that avidin is dispensable for resistance against Streptococcus agalactiae bacteremia in zebrafish.
rationale: Organism violation: The study is conducted entirely in zebrafish (Danio rerio), a teleost fish. Our eligibility protocol is strictly limited to mammalian laboratory animals (mice, rats, pigs, sheep, rabbits, etc.) and excludes non-mammalian organisms.
learning_pearl: Zebrafish Infection Model: Even when live pathogenic bacteria (Streptococcus agalactiae) are injected in vivo to model bacteremic infection, fish (zebrafish) are non-mammalian and must be EXCLUDED under EX-NOT-INVIVO!

title: The immunomodulatory effects of metformin in LPS-induced macrophages: an in vitro study
authors: Al-Rashed, F., Ahmad, Z., Tengholm, A., et al.
abstract: Metformin, a first-line biguanide for type 2 diabetes, possesses pleiotropic anti-inflammatory properties through AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) activation. We evaluated the direct immunomodulatory actions of metformin on macrophage polarization and cytokine release in an in vitro cell culture model of endotoxin shock. Murine RAW 264.7 macrophage cell lines and primary peritoneal macrophages harvested from C57BL/6 mice were cultured in vitro and stimulated with Escherichia coli LPS (100 ng/mL) with or without metformin pre-treatment (1–5 mM). Culture supernatants were harvested for ELISA, and intracellular signaling (AMPK phosphorylation, NF-κB p65 nuclear translocation, and iNOS/Arg-1 mRNA expressions) was determined by Western blotting and RT-qPCR. Metformin significantly suppressed LPS-stimulated NO, TNF-α, and IL-6 production in a dose-dependent manner and promoted an M2 anti-inflammatory phenotype. Metformin directly attenuates macrophage hyperinflammation in vitro.
rationale: In vitro study design: The study was performed entirely on cultured cell lines (RAW 264.7 macrophages) and harvested cells in culture plates without in vivo experimentation in living animals.
learning_pearl: In Vitro / Cell Culture Trap: Isolated macrophage cultures, RAW 264.7 cells, or in vitro cell assays lack whole-animal physiological systems and are excluded under EX-NOT-INVIVO.

title: Infection by Different Clades of Candidozyma auris in a Galleria mellonella Model: Determining Virulence Levels
authors: Carvalho, V. S., Rossi, S. A., Taborda, C. P., et al.
abstract: Candidozyma auris (formerly Candida auris) is an emerging multidrug-resistant fungal pathogen capable of causing life-threatening candidemia and systemic septic shock in hospitalized patients. Because mammalian infection experiments require specialized infrastructure, larvae of the greater wax moth, Galleria mellonella, have gained widespread adoption as an in vivo model for microbial virulence. We evaluated the lethal virulence of clinical C. auris isolates belonging to distinct geographic clades (South Asian, East Asian, South African, South American) in G. mellonella larvae. Sixth-instar larvae were inoculated with 1 × 10^6 CFU via the last left proleg and incubated at 37°C. Larval survival, fungal burden, and melanization scores were assessed daily for 7 days. Significant clade-dependent differences in survival were observed, with South Asian clade isolates inducing 80% larval mortality within 48 h. G. mellonella provides a rapid in vivo screen for C. auris virulence.
rationale: Organism violation: The study is conducted in wax moth larvae (Galleria mellonella, an insect/invertebrate). Our protocol strictly requires mammalian laboratory models.
learning_pearl: Invertebrate Model Trap: Galleria mellonella (wax moth larvae), Drosophila (fruit flies), and C. elegans (nematodes) are widely used infection models, but all non-mammalian organisms are EXCLUDED under EX-NOT-INVIVO!
